message.content:
The lion (*Panthera leo*) and the zebra (*Equus quagga*) belong to very different mammalian lineages—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore not a specific extinct species but rather the last common ancestor of the entire clade that contains both orders, which is the clade **Mammalia**.

In terms of evolutionary time, this ancestor lived roughly **200–250 million years ago**, during the late Triassic–early Jurassic period, when the first true mammals diverged from their reptile‑like synapsid ancestors. From that point onward, the lineages that would become the modern carnivores (including lions) and the odd‑toed ungulates (including zebras) split and evolved independently.

So, the common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all mammals—a synapsid that lived about 200–250 million years ago.
